course_name_original: Tecnologías y Paradigmas de la Programación
prerequisites: Programming courses from the first year (Introduction to Programming, Programming Methodology)
Computability from the first semester of the second year

learning_outcomes.text: Know and apply good practices for software design and implementation in order to alleviate and prevent software errors.
Know and apply error control mechanisms at runtime.
Know security mechanisms in the studied programming paradigms.
Develop an application according to the specifications of a given problem, ensuring the security conditions of the process and environment.
Know the mechanisms for evaluating software performance.
Evaluate the performance of a software development according to the paradigm, language, and environment.
Know the logical and functional programming paradigms.
Know the formal bases of logical and functional programming.
Develop a solution based on logical programming for a given problem specification.
Develop a solution based on functional programming for a given problem specification.
Know what a deductive database is.
Know the concept of a design pattern.
Apply pattern-based design to a given problem specification.
Evaluate the programming paradigm as well as the appropriate language for a given program specification.
Select the programming paradigm as well as the appropriate language for a given program specification.
Comprehend and apply the fundamental principles and basic techniques of real-time programming, extending from the OO paradigm to concurrency and event-oriented programming.

assessment_rules: For the ordinary assessment, the final theory grade (NotaT) is calculated as: max(10, max(ExT1, ExFT1) * 0.20 + max(ExT2, ExFT2) * 0.30 + max(ExT3, ExFT3) * 0.30 + max(ExT4, ExFT4) * 0.20 + PartT). The final practical grade (NotaP) is calculated as: max(10, max(ExP1, ExFP1) * 0.20 + max(ExP2, ExFP2) * 0.30 + max(ExP3, ExFP3) * 0.30 + max(ExP4, ExFP4) * 0.20 + PartP). If a minimum score of 4 is achieved in both blocks, the final grade is NotaT * 0.4 + NotaP * 0.6; otherwise, it is the minimum of the calculated grade and 4.0. For the extraordinary assessment, a single theoretical exam (ExT) and a single practical exam (ExP) are conducted, with NotaT = ExT and NotaP = ExP. To pass, a minimum score of 4 in both parts is required, otherwise the final grade is the minimum of (NotaT * 0.4 + NotaP * 0.6) and 4.0. Approved blocks from the ordinary call (grade >= 5) are retained.
